note.explanation: Protocols are rules for communication between devices. DNS looks up the IP address for a domain name, while DHCP automatically gives an IP address to a device on a network.
examples: Typing www.example.com in a browser: DNS translates the domain name to its IP address.
Connecting a device to Wi-Fi: DHCP assigns the device an IP address.
note.checkAnswer: DHCP automatically assigns IP addresses to devices on a network.
note.simple: DNS finds the address of a website. DHCP gives a connected device its network address.

mcqs.stem: What is a protocol in network communication?
rationales: Correct: protocols are sets of rules that govern data communication.
Incorrect: a router, rather than a protocol, connects networks and directs data.
Incorrect: storing web pages is not the definition of a protocol.
Incorrect: protocols do not assign domain names.

explain.title: Protocols
explain.body: Protocols are sets of rules that govern data communication. Devices use these rules to communicate. Common protocols include TCP/IP, HTTP, FTP and SMTP.

explain.title: HTTP
explain.body: HyperText Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is used for transferring web pages over the internet.

explain.title: DNS
explain.body: Domain Name System (DNS) translates domain names to IP addresses, making it easier for users to access websites.

explain.title: DHCP
explain.body: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) automatically assigns IP addresses to devices on a network, simplifying network management.

mistakes: Do not confuse DNS with DHCP: DNS translates domain names to IP addresses, while DHCP assigns IP addresses to devices.
Do not say HTTP automatically gives a device its address; that is DHCP's function.
When defining protocols, include their role in governing data communication.
For full marks, state what DHCP assigns and that it does so automatically.
